S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, and provide a complete incident report within 30 days. Incidents involving death, serious injury, evacuation, or substantial property damage must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk to their model or requires customer action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The 5% failure rate is the maximum performance benchmark for each model and an exceedance requires prompt corrective action; it does not by itself automatically prohibit sales or require withdrawal from the market. Provide results to customers of that model before purchase and to existing customers upon request. Results must not be withheld from customers.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect must support remote emergency shut-off... Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote shut-off within 6 years of the effective date where technically feasible... If retrofit is infeasible, the manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers and provide an equivalent risk-reduction measure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression designed to contain or control thermal events, tested to a regulator-approved protocol. Regulators may grant a time-limited, model-specific exemption where equivalent or greater protection is demonstrated.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and provide updates on corrective actions. A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the regulator may also require a recall or other corrective action where the risk warrants it.

document.section_notes: The final S2 sets a 5% benchmark at 55 °C but explicitly does not stop sales of models above it, so a flagship at 6.2% (Northwind's Hearth 10) can keep selling under corrective-action terms. S3 gives new units 24 months and a 6-year retrofit window for installed units, both longer than the answer key's acceptable limits, which favours Northwind's low remote shut-off share. S5 makes an 8-per-100,000 recall mandatory with no transition period, which would capture Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9, while S4's 36-month suppression lead time benefits Halcyon's higher suppression cost.
